intro: You've been thinking about it for a while — that cramped, awkward bathroom in your Merton home that just doesn't work anymore. Maybe the shower tray has seen better days, the tiles are cracked, or you're simply after something cleaner, more modern, and genuinely easier to keep on top of. A wet room installation is one of the most satisfying home improvements you can make, turning a functional but uninspiring space into something that feels genuinely luxurious. It's also a smart long-term investment — particularly in a borough like Merton, where property values reward well-executed renovations. This guide covers everything you need to know before getting started.
localContext: Merton's housing stock is wonderfully varied, and that variety has a real impact on how a wet room installation is planned and priced. Victorian terraces — common across areas like Colliers Wood, Wimbledon, and Mitcham — often have solid timber floor joists that need careful assessment before any wet room tanking or drainage work begins. These older homes can also have awkward bathroom dimensions and original plasterwork that requires specialist attention. Post-war properties, found throughout much of the borough, tend to have more straightforward floor structures but can present their own challenges around pipework routing and existing tile substrates. Newer builds and modern conversions are generally the easiest to work with, though space is often at a premium. It's also worth noting that Merton sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale build-up is a genuine concern. When specifying fittings — particularly shower heads, screens, and thermostatic valves — choosing products designed to resist scale and installing a water softener or inline filter is well worth discussing with your installer.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in Merton typically follows a clear sequence, though timelines and complexity vary depending on your property type and existing bathroom layout. The process begins with a thorough survey of the room — your installer will assess floor structure, drainage options, waterproofing requirements, and how existing plumbing can be adapted or extended. For most Merton properties, this survey stage is where the most important decisions are made, particularly around whether a pump-assisted drain or gravity-fed solution is appropriate given the floor depth available. Once design and materials are agreed, the existing bathroom is stripped out completely. Floor preparation is then critical — a former or screed is used to create the correct fall towards the drain, ensuring water flows away efficiently without pooling. Full tanking follows, applying a specialist waterproof membrane across the floor, walls, and any joints, which is the single most important step in making sure your wet room stays watertight for years to come. Tiling, screen installation, and fitting of fixtures — including your shower valve, head, and any heated towel rails — come next. Finally, sanitary ware is installed, silicone finished, and the room is left to cure before use. From start to finish, most wet room projects in Merton take between five and ten working days for a standard-sized bathroom.
pricing: In Merton, a fully fitted wet room installation typically costs between £6,500 and £12,000, depending on the size of the space, the complexity of the build, and the quality of materials chosen. A straightforward installation in a modern property with good access and simple drainage might come in towards the lower end of that range, while a Victorian terrace requiring floor reinforcement, bespoke tanking, and premium fixtures will sit towards the top. Underfloor heating, frameless screens, and designer sanitaryware all add to the final figure. Labour typically accounts for around 40–50% of the total cost in Merton, reflecting the skill level involved and the borough's position in Greater London. Always get at least two or three detailed quotes.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who works regularly in Merton makes a practical difference. They'll be familiar with the construction quirks found in local Victorian terraces and post-war housing, understand typical planning considerations in the borough, and have established relationships with local suppliers — which can mean faster access to materials and more competitive pricing. A local installer is also easier to get back if there's ever a follow-up question or a minor snagging issue down the line. Wet room installation is a significant investment, and having someone with genuine knowledge of Merton's properties handling the work gives you confidence from survey to sign-off.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older Victorian property in Merton?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires careful planning. Victorian homes in Merton often have timber joists that need to be assessed and sometimes reinforced before a wet room former and drainage system can be installed correctly. A good installer will survey the floor structure early in the process and advise on any preparation work needed before tanking begins.

faqs.q: How do I deal with limescale on wet room fittings in Merton?
faqs.a: Because Merton has moderately hard water, limescale on shower heads, screens, and valves is a real issue over time. Specifying fittings with easy-clean nozzles, using a daily shower spray, and considering an inline scale inhibitor on the water supply to your shower will all help. Some homeowners in the borough also opt for a whole-house water softener when renovating.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Merton?
faqs.a: Most standard wet room projects in Merton take between five and ten working days from strip-out to completion. More complex jobs — particularly in older properties requiring floor reinforcement or extensive re-routing of pipework — can take up to two weeks. Your installer should give you a clear programme before work begins so you can plan accordingly.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a Merton property?
faqs.a: Generally, yes. In Merton's competitive property market, a well-designed wet room — particularly one fitted with quality materials and a timeless finish — is viewed positively by buyers and can increase perceived value. It's especially appealing in properties where the existing bathroom is dated or poorly laid out. The key is using a skilled installer and choosing a design that feels considered rather than trendy.
